title: Aviation Maintenance Technology: Airframe
award: Certificate of Achievement: 18  or greater semester(or 27  or greater quarter) u

program.section_heading: Aviation Maintenance Technology: Airframe - Certificate of Achievement
outcomes: Successfully demonstrate the ability to pass the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) knowledge, oral, practical and written examinations in Airframe subjects. Leading to a certificate to take the Airframe FAA written and practical tests.
Demonstrate a working knowledge and mechanical ability with metal aircraft structures, cabin atmospherice control systems, aircraft instruments, naviagation systems, fuel systems.
Demonstrate the ability to research, prepare and determine applicability of aircraft inspections and aerodynamics.
Communicate both in writing and verbally about aircraft general maintenance concepts and processes using technical terms, to both professional and administrative audiences.
Demonstrate the ability to display and apply proper behavior reflecting satisfactory safe work habits and ethics to fulfill program requirements and confidence to prepare for employment.
careers: repair or sales of aircraft accessories

notes: AMT 100 and AMT 101 are both printed with the title 'General Aircraft Technology (Active)' and 9 units; both listed as required, and the stated 45 units equals 9+9+13.5+13.5. AMT 100 is not in the closed list; reviewer may check whether it is a duplicate/renumbered course.
AMT 190 is marked (Historical) in the catalog and listed under Recommended Electives with Units: 0.
Outcomes are copied verbatim including printed typos ('atmospherice', 'naviagation').
Careers include both listed occupations and fields of employment named in the program summary.
